schema: cs2-broken/2 - read by the bridge (BROKEN_FILE) and by site/broken-maps.py
source: CS2 workshop load sweep v1+v2 of 2026-10-03 on engine 1.41.8.8, every item on the list and in the spare pool loaded on the server; the 10 uncertain items resolved from their download contents

fields.maps: real maps that crash or freeze the server, and (crashes 0) maps that break something else: advertise another server or post a gambling ad (2026-10-24), crash the players' games, or break the players' HUD (2026-11-01). The bridge reads id, crashes and reason: crashes > 0 makes its confirm say 'crashed N of N test loads', and reason is what the HUD's card, the confirm and the site say about the map (since Over Strike 2; 'is on the broken list' without one). rank is the !map number (null: not on the list), evidence is the site's banner text
fields.packs: workshop items with no playable map in them, refused outright in chat by id and name. The bridge reads id and name; kind (pack | empty | stub | legacy: a CS:GO-era upload with no CS2 map), evidence (confirmed by test | identified from description | identified from its Workshop file: the Workshop names a CS:GO file, 2026-11-01), phrase, detail, preview and description are for the site's Not maps tab. list says where it was found (live | spare | newer | tail | sync | scrape: the first scrape of 2026-09-17); formerRank is the !map number the item had until the 2026-10-03 rank-stable refresh
fields.removed: maps gone from the Workshop: nobody can download them, so every client gets ERROR 15 and nobody can join while one is on. Refused outright in chat (and from the HUD), never rolled or queued. The bridge reads id (and verdict: removed | hidden | banned, default removed); rank, name, since and evidence are for the site's banner. A seed: the bridge's daily Workshop check (/data/removed.json) overrides it for every id it has checked, so a map that comes back is unblocked without editing this file
fields.blocked: maps blocked for good, each for its own reason: refused outright in chat by id, URL or name (and from the HUD and !previous), never rolled or queued, left out of the HUD's map browser. The bridge reads id, name, map (the map name the server logs) and reason; the refusal reads '<name> (<id>) <reason> - it is blocked.'
